title: Enterprise Cloud-Managed LLM Deployment Modes (PAYGO vs PTU) vs. Self-Hosted Kubernetes (AKS/EKS + KAITO/vLLM) TCO Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: 100% Serverless `PAYGO` Token API at High Sustained Enterprise Volume (`120B Tokens/Mo`)
tiers.architecture: Routing 100% of steady high-volume production traffic + bursts to per-token Serverless PAYGO endpoints without PTU or self-hosted pools

tiers.tier: Tier 2: 100% Peak-Sized Cloud Provisioned Throughput (`PTU` / Bedrock Provisioned) Without Burst Spillover
tiers.architecture: Buying enough fixed monthly PTUs to cover the absolute Monday 10:00 AM peak (leaving 68% of PTU capacity idle overnight/weekends)

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Premature Self-Hosted `AKS / EKS + vLLM` for Low/Medium Spiky Workloads (Ignoring Hidden SRE FTE Cost)
tiers.architecture: Hiring 3 full-time K8s/GPU SREs ($55K/mo fully loaded payroll) + paying 24x7 GPU node bills before workload crosses the 25B token/mo break-even threshold

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Volume-Inflection Hybrid (`P55 Base PTU + PAYGO Burst` for Frontier + `AKS/KAITO Self-Hosted vLLM` for High-Volume Open-Weight `>30B Tok/Mo`)
tiers.architecture: Size Cloud PTUs at the 55th-percentile diurnal baseline + spill bursts to PAYGO; offload steady `>30B tok/mo` open-weight/distilled workloads to AKS + KAITO/vLLM

scenarios.scenario: The 3 Cost-Inflection Points: `Serverless PAYGO` vs. `Provisioned PTU` vs. `Self-Hosted K8s (AKS + vLLM)`
scenarios.question: At what exact monthly token volume and utilization factor should an enterprise switch from Serverless PAYGO to Reserved PTUs, or to Self-Hosted Kubernetes (`AKS / EKS + KAITO / vLLM`)?
scenarios.model_answer: Follow the **Three-Zone Break-Even Law (Including Hidden SRE Payroll!)**: (1) **`< 5B Tokens/Mo` or Spiky (`< 35%` 24x7 duty cycle)** -> **100% Serverless PAYGO** (zero idle waste, 0 SRE FTE); (2) **`5B–30B Tokens/Mo` on Frontier Models (`>= 50%` duty cycle)** -> **Base `PTU` (sized at P55 load) + `PAYGO` Spillover** (deterministic 480ms P99 TTFT + 35%–50% savings); (3) **`> 30B Tokens/Mo` on Open-Weight/Distilled Models (`8B–70B`) with `>= 1` K8s Platform Engineer** -> **Self-Hosted `AKS/EKS + KAITO/vLLM`** (`$0.72 / 1M tokens`, `$106K/mo` total TCO including SRE FTE!)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 overpays $322K/mo on PAYGO at 120B tokens/mo; Tier 3 self-hosts Kubernetes too early and burns $55K/mo on 3 GPU SREs for a small workload.

scenarios.scenario: Why Sizing `PTU` for 100% Peak Load Wastes 68% of Your Reservation (`The P55 Base + PAYGO Spillover Law`)
scenarios.question: Enterprise peak load at 10:00 AM Monday requires 220 PTUs, but average 24x7 load is only 95 PTUs; buying 220 PTUs costs $244K/month
scenarios.model_answer: Never size PTUs for the 100th-percentile peak! Provision **110 PTUs (`P55` baseline load, running at `88%` 24x7 utilization)** and configure the AI Gateway (`Azure APIM / Envoy`) to spill the top 15% daytime peak requests to **Serverless PAYGO** on `HTTP 429` (`0.0%` throttling, saving `$138K/mo` vs peak-sized PTUs)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 buys 220 PTUs for a 2-hour morning peak, leaving 68% of reserved capacity idle overnight and on weekends.

scenarios.scenario: Accounting for the 'Hidden $55,000/Month Kubernetes GPU SRE Tax' in Self-Hosted TCO Models
scenarios.question: A developer calculates that 8x H100 GPUs cost $45K/mo vs $70K/mo on Cloud API and claims self-hosting saves $25K/mo—but forgets driver upgrades, CVE patching, and 24x7 on-call
scenarios.model_answer: Raw GPU cloud rental is only 60% of self-hosted TCO! Maintaining raw K8s + NVIDIA GPU Operator + vLLM + Prometheus + PagerDuty requires **2.5–3.0 FTEs (`~$55,000/month` payroll)** unless automated via **Managed K8s AI Operators (`AKS KAITO / GKE Autopilot / AWS HyperPod`)** which reduce operational burden to `1.0 FTE` (`$18K/mo`)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 ignores $55K/mo in SRE engineering salaries when comparing raw GPU instance prices against managed APIs.

scenarios.scenario: Contractual Latency SLA (`P99 TTFT`) & Noisy-Neighbor Isolation (`PTU` vs. `PAYGO`)
scenarios.question: During global product launches, multi-tenant Serverless PAYGO P99 TTFT spikes from 600ms to 2,380ms with 14.5% HTTP 429 rate-limit errors
scenarios.model_answer: Pin latency-critical customer-facing Copilots (`P0`) to **Dedicated `PTU` / Reserved Self-Hosted GPU Pools (`420ms` guaranteed P99 TTFT)**, and route asynchronous/internal `P2` workloads to PAYGO or nighttime PTU backfill
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 puts mission-critical live customer voice/chat on best-effort PAYGO endpoints (`2,380ms` P99 TTFT spikes).

perturbation_checks.check: Workload Volume Drops by 60% During Seasonal Business Slowdown
perturbation_checks.perturbed: $68,000/mo TCO (PAYGO Burst Drops to $0 & Self-Hosted Spot/On-Demand Scales In Automatically)
perturbation_checks.change_pts: -$38,000/mo Elastic Savings (vs $0 Saved in Fixed Tier 2)

perturbation_checks.check: Adding a New Department Workload Requiring an Open-Weight Custom 8B/70B Model
perturbation_checks.perturbed: $0.64 / 1M Cost (Mounted as an Additional Multi-LoRA / KAITO Workspace on Existing AKS Pool)

key_findings: Tier 4 (P55 Base PTU + PAYGO Burst for 40% frontier traffic + AKS/KAITO Self-Hosted vLLM for 60% high-volume open-weight traffic) achieves $0.72/1M blended token cost, 420ms P99 TTFT, 0.0% 429 throttling, and $106K/mo full TCO including SRE FTE (-67.1% vs 100% PAYGO and -56.6% vs 100% peak PTU).

True TCO must include Platform SRE FTE payroll (~$18.5K/mo per FTE): self-hosting Kubernetes GPUs only beats managed cloud APIs once steady open-weight volume exceeds ~25B–30B tokens/month and `AKS KAITO` reduces ops to <=1.0 FTE.
Provisioning cloud PTUs at the 55th-percentile baseline load (`P55`) and overflowing peaks to PAYGO eliminates the 68% overnight idle waste of peak-sized PTU reservations.
